_source: The shared vocabulary of the config-search report surfaces. CANONICAL COPY.
_mirror: web/src/lexicon.json is a byte-identical mirror, imported by the React dashboard (which cannot read the skill dir at build time). scripts/test_build.py fails if the two drift.
_why: config-search renders the same runs twice -- the standalone HTML report (report.py + figures.py + report/template.html) and the React dashboard (web/src). They had grown two vocabularies for one set of numbers ('Speed per user' / 'Per-user rate' / 'tok/s per user') and, worse, two ranking objectives for 'What to run'. Both now read their labels and their objective from this file, so a reader moving between the two surfaces sees one set of words and one recommendation.

objective.label: tok/s per GPU
objective.rule: Among the SERVABLE runs at one load, the operating point is the run with the highest tok/s per GPU; ties break on fleet tok/s, then tok/s per user, then run id (so the pick is deterministic, not iteration-order dependent).
objective.why: tok/s per GPU is the efficiency half of the dual-Pareto objective the search optimises and picks its own winner on, so the 'What to run' table, the recommendation card and the search winner all rank on one number. Ranking by per-user rate instead made the table recommend the fastest-per-user shape while the card above recommended the most efficient one: on kimi-k2.5 that is TP8+EP at 23 tok/s/GPU versus the winner's TP4xDP2+EP at 67.
objective.blurb: One row per load: the most efficient configuration that still held the floor there, and the flags to deploy it with. Rows are ranked on tok/s per GPU — the objective the search picks its winner on. Pick the load you expect, then read the flags off it.
objective.none: No run held the interactivity floor, so there is no operating point to recommend. The full run log lists every run and why each one missed.

conc.label: sessions
conc.help: Concurrent sessions — simultaneous users/requests — at this operating point.

pu.label: tok/s per user
pu.help: Output tokens per second a single session sees — the interactivity each caller feels. On a p99 basis, the same basis as the interactivity floor.

cl.label: tok/s fleet
cl.help: Total output tokens per second across every instance and GPU in the deployment — the whole config's serving capacity.

tpg.label: tok/s per GPU
tpg.help: Fleet throughput divided by total GPUs — how efficiently each GPU is used.

itl.label: TPOT p99
itl.help: Time per output token (p99), a.k.a. inter-token latency (ITL): the gap between output tokens. Lower feels snappier.

ttft.label: TTFT p99
ttft.help: Time to first token (p99): how long a caller waits before the reply starts streaming.

e2e.label: E2E p99
e2e.help: End-to-end latency (p99): total time from request to the last output token.

p95.label: E2E p95
p95.help: End-to-end latency of the slowest 95% of sessions — the tail check on a fast-looking config.

sched.label: queue delay p99
sched.help: Scheduling delay (p99): time a request spent queued before admission.

hit.label: prefix hit
hit.help: Fraction of prompt tokens served from the prefix cache.

al.label: acceptance length
al.help: Mean tokens accepted per verification step (AL), from the registry's measured acceptance profile. Under drafting one step emits AL tokens, so the per-user rate is AL x 1000 / ITL p99 rather than 1000 / ITL p99.

series.label: configuration
series.help: The serving topology — GPUs, tensor/data/expert parallelism and instance count.

variant.label: knob delta
variant.help: How this run's engine and routing knobs differ from its topology group's baseline.

tp.label: tensor parallel
tp.help: How many GPUs each copy of the model is split across.

dp.label: data parallel
dp.help: How many data-parallel replicas each instance runs.

epw.label: expert-parallel width
epw.help: How many ranks the MoE experts are sharded over (derived as tp x dp); off when expert parallelism is disabled.

ni.label: instances
ni.help: How many independent model replicas serve the fleet.

ok.label: servable
ok.help: Whether the run held the interactivity floor and every SLO.

src.label: run source
src.help: Which search phase produced the run.

nodes.label: nodes
nodes.help: How many 8-GPU nodes the pool spans; past one, collectives cross a fabric.

pd.label: prefill/decode
pd.help: Whether prefill and decode share instances (colocated) or run on separate pools (disagg).

route.label: routing
route.help: The llm-d EndpointPicker configuration that picks an instance for each request; "default" is the router's own built-in one.

scorers.label: route scorers
scorers.help: The scorers the routing policy ranks instances with.

admit.label: admission
admit.help: The policy deciding whether a request is admitted or shed.

a2a.label: MoE dispatch
a2a.help: The all-to-all backend that moves tokens to their experts.

mnbt.label: max batched tokens
mnbt.help: Engine cap on the tokens in one batch (--max-num-batched-tokens).

gmu.label: gpu mem util
gmu.help: Fraction of each GPU's memory the engine may use (--gpu-memory-utilization).

mtp.label: draft tokens
mtp.help: Speculative-decoding draft depth K (engine.speculative.num_spec_tokens); 0 is off.

spec.label: drafter
spec.help: The speculative method the model drafts with (dspark, mtp, eagle3, …); empty when drafting is off.

axes.cl_log: aggregate output tok/s delivered by the cluster (log)
axes.max_conc: highest concurrency served inside every limit

operating_curve.title: The operating curve, and where it stops
operating_curve.caption: Each configuration trades tok/s per user for tok/s fleet, until it falls off a cliff. One line per configuration, walking the load up; the number beside each marker is the session count. Filled markers hold the interactivity floor, hollow ones break a limit. The dashed line is the floor itself.
operating_curve.read: One line per configuration, walking the load up. Flat is good — it means adding sessions has not yet slowed anyone down. Where a line turns down is its knee: the first load that breaks the floor.

per_user_vs_load.title: tok/s per user vs load
per_user_vs_load.caption: Each configuration trades tok/s per user for tok/s fleet, until it falls off a cliff. One line per configuration, walking the load up. Filled markers hold the interactivity floor, hollow ones break a limit.
per_user_vs_load.read: One line per configuration, walking the load up. Flat is good — it means adding sessions has not yet slowed anyone down. The violet line marks that configuration's knee, the first load that breaks the floor.

efficiency_interactivity.title: Efficiency ↔ interactivity
efficiency_interactivity.caption: tok/s per GPU against tok/s per user, one point per run — the two halves of the search objective, plotted against each other.
efficiency_interactivity.read: Each point is one run: x is what one caller feels, y is how much each GPU delivers (so configurations compare regardless of how many GPUs they use). Up and to the right is better for everyone; filled points hold the interactivity floor, hollow ones break it. A faint line connects a configuration's runs in load order, so you can trace where adding sessions takes it.

latency_vs_load.title: Latency vs load
latency_vs_load.caption: The latency behind the per-user cliff, as the load climbs.
latency_vs_load.read: Lower is better, and the interactivity floor is a ceiling on this number, so a line crossing its knee is what makes tok/s per user fall.

tail_scatter.title: Why the fastest-looking configuration can be the wrong one
tail_scatter.caption: tok/s per user against the slowest 95% of session latencies. Every run; crosses break a limit. A configuration pushed past its cliff reports a lower tok/s per user AND a longer tail — the two move together, so the tail is a faithful independent check.
tail_scatter.read: An independent check that a fast-looking configuration is not fast only because it dropped or queued requests.

scale_bars.title: How far each configuration scales
scale_bars.caption: Highest concurrency each configuration serves inside every limit. The cross marks the first load that breaks one. Identical hardware, identical workload.
scale_bars.read: One bar per configuration: how many sessions it carries before any limit binds.
